git.source_digest_rule: sha256 over name+bytes of src/trading_bot/research/edge01/*.py, scripts/edge01_run.py and scripts/edge01_verify.py, with CRLF folded to LF so the digest does not depend on the checkout's line endings

mode: deterministic backtest over the local historical corpus: the frozen 4h trend ruleset, unchanged, re-measured and read for sensitivity; 0 orders, 0 credentials, 0 network calls

experiment.reproduces: reports/edge-recovery/WP-EDGE-01/oos-trend-4h/OOS_TREND.json — the frozen ruleset is measured again with the same harness and compared with the published figures; a moved reading fails the run instead of being restated
experiment.question: WP-EDGE-01 refused the frozen 4h trend ruleset for one reason: the largest winning trade was 0.7987 of the OOS net against a 0.50 limit. Beyond that single number — how much of the OOS reading survives dropping the largest winner (and the three largest), which asset and which regime carry it, does it survive the adverse cost plane, and what interval does the sample support once the trades' own autocorrelation is taken into account?

uncertainty.hac: Newey-West (Bartlett-weighted) standard error of the mean trade net, with lag = floor(4 * (n/100)^(2/9)) declared here; two-sided 95% interval from the Student-t critical value by the Cornish-Fisher expansion
uncertainty.bootstrap: stationary block bootstrap over the trades in time order: a new block starts with probability 1/block_length, block_length = 5, 5000 resamples, xorshift64* PRNG from a declared seed, percentile interval of the mean

decision_rule.decisive_failures: a powered sample in which the edge is CONTRADICTED: OOS net <= 0, or the net after dropping the single largest winner <= 0 (the reading is one trade), or fewer than min_positive_assets single-asset books positive, or the HAC interval's upper end <= 0 (the sample says the expectancy is not positive)
decision_rule.inconclusive_failures: a powered sample in which the declared requirements are not met but the edge is not contradicted: concentration above the 0.50 limit while the leave-one-out net stays positive, an interval that contains 0, the adverse cost plane below 0 while the base plane is above it, fewer than min_positive_periods positive periods, or a candidate drawdown that is not below buy & hold

meaning.ADMIT_PAPER: every declared requirement met on OOS, including the concentration limit
meaning.REJECT: a powered sample in which the edge is contradicted
meaning.INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE: a powered sample the requirements cannot decide, or an unpowered one

proposal_not_applied.what: a size-aware concentration criterion (e.g. the share measured against the sum of the top-k winners, or against gross profit instead of net)
proposal_not_applied.status: a proposal for a NEW pre-registered experiment with its own corpus split; it is NOT applied to this run, and the run is judged against 0.50

decision_rule.not_claimed: PAPER here means the evidence supports wiring the frozen ruleset into the paper pipeline; it is not a profitability claim, not a live-trading authorisation and not a certification. No capital is at risk in this experiment.

wp_admission_criteria.note: Initial thresholds for WP-EDGE-01, recorded before the campaign ran. They are NOT an approved profitability bar; they are the minimum evidence needed to avoid calling noise an edge. The cost-stress criterion (OOS net still positive at 2x fees) is stated here rather than inferred from the measured results.

reproduction.note: the frozen ruleset, corpus, cost components and risk policy are unchanged: the recomputed figures equal the published ones exactly

corpus_coverage.note: the design windows (DEV 2019-2023, VAL 2024, OOS 2025-01 -> 2026-02-28) consume the frozen 4h corpus to its last complete bar; the only bars left are 5 mop-up bars (0.83 days), far below the declared 30-day minimum for a usable extra period, so no unused independent sample exists inside this corpus

reasons: the largest single trade is 0.80 of the oos net

meta.timeframe: 1d (aggregated from 1h shards; a day exists only when its 24 contiguous hours do)
meta.rule: benchmark BTC daily close against its own 200-day EMA, with that EMA's 20-day change deciding trend from range: BULL when close > EMA200 and the EMA rose over the last 20 days, BEAR when close < EMA200 and it fell, SIDEWAYS otherwise, UNDEFINED while either input is still warming up. This is the project's existing convention (trading_bot/research/swing/backtest.py::build_regimes), reused rather than re-invented; it is a market label for reporting, never a signal.

limitations: the ruleset is untuned and frozen and VAL/OOS were already read for it in WP-EDGE-01, so this is a decomposition and a sensitivity analysis of the published run, not a second independent sample
the concentration criterion is the same 0.50 WP-EDGE-01 froze; relaxing it is proposed as a new experiment and is deliberately NOT applied here

the frozen corpus ends at the last bar of the OOS window (2026-02-28), so no unused independent period exists: an additional period needs a new corpus, which the 15m feed could supply but only as a new pre-registered experiment
the HAC interval is asymptotic and the block bootstrap resamples 52 trades: both widen the reading honestly, neither turns 52 observations into a large sample
the candidate risks a fixed share of equity per trade while buy & hold is fully invested, so the comparison is on the same window and cost plane, not on the same capital utilisation
long side only (spot); no historical order book; nothing is wired into PAPER
